tagline: Over the Sunol Grade and up the valleys.
intro: From Mission Boulevard in Fremont, Interstate 680 turns abruptly northeast into the hills of the Coast Ranges, crosses Mission Pass, also known as the Sunol Grade, and comes down into the Sunol Valley, running with Highway 84 for a short way near Sunol. From there it heads north-northwest through the valleys, past Pleasanton and Dublin, to the Contra Costa line.

After the September 11 attacks someone painted a US flag on a large piece of concrete on a hill along the grade. It stayed there nine years, until Caltrans painted it over, nobody having asked permission in the first place.

moments.title: Sunol Water Temple
moments.text: Willis Polk's 1910 ring of twelve Corinthian columns, modeled on the Temple of Vesta at Tivoli, marks where three underground water sources meet, and half of San Francisco's water once flowed through it.

moments.title: Sunol
moments.text: The town once elected a dog named Bosco its mayor, which the People's Daily held up in 1990 as a failing of American elections, and his statue sits in front of the post office.

moments.title: Pleasanton
moments.text: Before it was Pleasanton it was Alisal, a bandit refuge nicknamed the Most Desperate Town in the West, and the present spelling is apparently a clerk's typo for General Pleasonton.
